reference: No GNU command has this loadable's argv or output contract: auditctl/ausearch operate through a different CLI and emit different formats. Contract expectations use Bash's documented type/help builtins, Linux Audit UAPI message type numbers, and the documented pinned map plus 9-field TSV encoding. Decoder records below are independently constructed from fixed payload fields, decimal timestamp arithmetic, and the documented unknown-type and tab/newline escaping rules; no candidate output is used as an oracle.
coverage: Static builtin availability and Bash help metadata with PATH empty.
Known Linux Audit message type name/number lookups and unknown lookup behavior.
decode-text timestamp conversion, quoted lifted fields, and retained key/value fields.
Unknown numeric message preservation and missing-field defaults.
Tab/newline escaping that keeps each decoded message on one TSV line.
Relative output-file append behavior for decode-text.
exclusions: There is no GNU CLI with matching decode-text, typename, typenum, or canonical rule-argument behavior, so these are honest contract cases rather than fabricated parity comparisons.

Kernel netlink operations are deferred: they require an audit-enabled disposable VM, audit capabilities, and controlled baseline/cleanup for global audit state. No live status, rule, enablement, or daemon operation is claimed as passed.

cases.purpose: Confirm the compiled builtin remains available with an empty executable path and that Bash help exposes the documented audit verbs and pure lookup/decoder operations.
cases.script:
PATH=
[[ $(type -t audit) == builtin ]]
help audit > audit-help.txt
IFS= read -r synopsis < audit-help.txt
[[ $synopsis == 'audit: audit' ]]
header_doc=0
status_doc=0
decode_doc=0
type_doc=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  [[ $line == *'NETLINK_AUDIT consumer for the bash-os audit engine (AUDIT-6.2).'* ]] && header_doc=1
  [[ $line == *'audit status [-V VAR]'* ]] && status_doc=1
  [[ $line == *'audit decode-text TYPE PAYLOAD [-o FILE]'* ]] && decode_doc=1
  [[ $line == *'pinned AUDIT_* map.'* ]] && type_doc=1
done < audit-help.txt
[[ $header_doc == 1 && $status_doc == 1 && $decode_doc == 1 && $type_doc == 1 ]]
printf 'builtin\nhelp-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check representative Linux Audit UAPI message numbers across syscall, configuration, user-authentication, and anomaly event families.
cases.script:
[[ $(audit typenum SYSCALL) == 1300 ]]
[[ $(audit typenum EXECVE) == 1309 ]]
[[ $(audit typenum CONFIG_CHANGE) == 1305 ]]
[[ $(audit typenum USER_AUTH) == 1100 ]]
[[ $(audit typenum USER_LOGIN) == 1112 ]]
[[ $(audit typenum ANOM_LOGIN_FAILURES) == 2100 ]]
printf '1300 1309 1305 1100 1112 2100\n'

cases.purpose: Check reverse lookups for pinned message numbers from the same independent Linux Audit UAPI families.
cases.script:
[[ $(audit typename 1300) == SYSCALL ]]
[[ $(audit typename 1309) == EXECVE ]]
[[ $(audit typename 1100) == USER_AUTH ]]
[[ $(audit typename 2100) == ANOM_LOGIN_FAILURES ]]
printf 'SYSCALL EXECVE USER_AUTH ANOM_LOGIN_FAILURES\n'

cases.purpose: Verify an unpinned numeric type prints UNKNOWN and returns failure, as specified by the type lookup contract.
cases.script:
if result=$(audit typename 9999); then exit 90; else status=$?; fi
[[ $status == 1 && $result == UNKNOWN ]]
printf 'UNKNOWN (status %s)\n' "$status"

cases.purpose: Verify an unpinned symbolic name is rejected with failure and no stdout instead of being assigned a guessed number.
cases.script:
if result=$(audit typenum NOT_AUDIT_TYPE); then exit 90; else status=$?; fi
[[ $status == 1 && -z $result ]]
printf 'unknown-name-rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Decode a fixed SYSCALL payload and independently check timestamp milliseconds, serial, quoted auid/uid/pid/exe/key extraction, and the remaining key/value tail.
cases.script: audit decode-text 1300 'audit(5.007:12): arch=c000003e syscall=59 success=yes auid=1000 uid=1001 pid=77 exe="/bin/a shell" key="exec watch" comm="shell"' -o -
cases.stdout: SYSCALL	5007	12	1000	1001	77	/bin/a shell	exec watch	arch=c000003e syscall=59 success=yes comm="shell"

cases.purpose: Check that an unpinned numeric event is retained as UNKNOWN with its numeric type in the kv tail, while absent lifted columns use the documented dash defaults.
Verify tabs and newlines inside a quoted audit value are percent-escaped so a message remains one nine-column TSV record.
Exercise decode-text -o with a relative private fixture file: existing contents must remain and two decoded records must be appended in order.
cases.script:
printf 'seed\n' > records.tsv
audit decode-text 1300 'audit(1.002:3): success=yes' -o records.tsv
audit decode-text 1302 'audit(1.004:5): name="file"' -o records.tsv
mapfile -t rows < records.tsv
[[ ${#rows[@]} == 3 ]]
[[ ${rows[0]} == seed ]]
[[ ${rows[1]} == $'SYSCALL\t1002\t3\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tsuccess=yes' ]]
[[ ${rows[2]} == $'PATH\t1004\t5\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tname="file"' ]]
printf 'append-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Cover status and list-rules netlink read behavior against a controlled audit kernel state.
cases.reason: No driver runs a case with CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the initial user and PID namespaces, and no controller records audit status/rules around a case. The image has no auditctl reference. Only the unprivileged refusal path is reachable with existing drivers and it is not asserted. Missing capability: CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the initial user and PID namespaces. An unprivileged fixture cannot observe the obligation: audit_netlink_ok() returns ECONNREFUSED in any non-initial user namespace (legacy bwrap, USERNS) and EPERM for uid 2000 without CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the plain driver; audit state is global, not namespaced.

cases.purpose: Cover set-enabled, add-rule, and del-rule encoding plus kernel acknowledgement and resulting rule state.
cases.reason: Rule mutation needs CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the initial user and PID namespaces plus snapshot/restore of global audit state; no driver provides that, and no reference auditctl is installed. Unprivileged argument-validation paths exist in the candidate but are not asserted. Missing capability: CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the initial user and PID namespaces. An unprivileged fixture cannot observe the obligation: audit_netlink_ok() returns ECONNREFUSED in any non-initial user namespace (legacy bwrap, USERNS) and EPERM for uid 2000 without CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the plain driver; audit state is global, not namespaced.

cases.purpose: Cover run registration, bounded event collection, decode integration, and cleanup of the audit daemon PID.
cases.reason: Consuming events requires being the registered audit daemon (CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL, initial user+PID ns, no competing auditd), a controller-installed rule, fixture-triggered events and pid/enabled restore. No driver provides that. Only the decoder is covered, with synthetic payloads. Missing capability: CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the initial user and PID namespaces. An unprivileged fixture cannot observe the obligation: audit_netlink_ok() returns ECONNREFUSED in any non-initial user namespace (legacy bwrap, USERNS) and EPERM for uid 2000 without CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the plain driver; audit state is global, not namespaced.

cases.purpose: An empty local payload encodes a nine-column record with zero timestamp/serial and missing lifted-field defaults.
A missing private output parent fails before emitting a record; no netlink operation is invoked.
